cohort: 359 neonates with symptoms and signs of sepsis who presented to the pediatric emergency care unit of Mulago national referral hospital from mid-January to end of December 2018
finding: Staphylococcus aureus was the most common cause of culture-positive neonatal sepsis, and cesarean delivery was strongly associated with an increased risk of culture-positive sepsis.
mod_finding: Cesarean section delivery was strongly associated with culture-positive sepsis.
